_note: One calibration of record (sprint 029 ticket 006, TL-02/TL-11). camlink.py loads this file and registers a mount with the aprilcam daemon ONLY on an explicit --register call; robotlink.py's radio_address() reads/derives from it. mount_yaw_residual_deg is the sub-degree PHYSICAL mount skew ONLY -- the fixed +90 deg AprilCam front-edge-to-hat convention (.claude/rules/tag-yaw-is-the-front-edge-not-the-hat.md) is never stored here; it is added back in code, once, by camlink.mount_yaw_rad() (for daemon registration) and field.robot_heading_from_tag_yaw() (for a raw, unregistered tag reading).

field._note: Fixed field furniture, not a robot -- not subject to the TL-02 remount-overwrite hazard. Height-only mount (drives camera parallax correction only; no forward direction, so no yaw convention applies). Register once per daemon session with `camlink.py --register field`. Tag 10 sits over the NW dot (-50, 30), tag 11 over the SW dot (-50, -30) -- permanent ground truth in every frame.

vevov._provenance: MEASURED vevov 2026-09-02 on main-playfield. Re-measure after any tag remount, camera move, or robot change.
vevov._mount_yaw_note: robot heading = tag yaw + 90 (fixed convention) + this residual. Fitted from a translation probe, not assumed: the two candidate conventions differ by 180 deg and picking wrong is how a robot ends up in a rail. Was stored pre-sprint-029 as the absolute heading_offset_deg (91.11616234175443 = 90 + this); TL-11 split the fixed convention back out.
vevov._radio_note: MEASURED 2026-08-30 (.claude/rules/playfield-testing.md fleet table); also the base-5 name-derived pair (make_deploy.derive_radio_from_name('vevov')) -- kept explicit here since this is the file robotlink.radio_address() reads first.
vevov._lever_note: Tag 53 relative to the centre of rotation, in the TAG frame. Solved from an in-place pivot triple, least squares over tag = centre + R(yaw)*lever: residual 0.28 mm rms, and the three implied centres agreed to 0.7 mm, which is the proof the robot pivoted in place. The raw tag swings 68 mm across a pivot, so an uncorrected trace carries that at every corner.
vevov._parallax_note: The tag rides 11.8 cm above the field, so the camera reports every DISPLACEMENT scaled by this about its own nadir. Divide any camera distance by it for truth. MEASURED as 1.1167 +- 0.0022 over three 60 cm legs driven in opposing directions; implies a camera height near 113 cm. Closure measured at equal heading still needs it, since closure is a displacement.

tovez._provenance: mount_yaw_residual_deg MEASURED tovez 2026-09-04, captures/bench-acceptance-029-20260904d/heading-probe.log: with the tag registered at the fleet -90 deg convention the daemon reported yaw -165.8 deg while a 5 cm MOVE_X probe displaced the tag 4.87 cm at bearing +11.4 deg (bearing - reported yaw = +177.3 deg). The plate on tovez is therefore mounted 180 deg from the fleet convention (its 'up' points backward); the residual records that physical fact until the plate is remounted, at which point set it back to 0. mount_x_cm sign flipped to +4.1 for the same reason (the tag sits in FRONT of the centre in the 2026-09-04 deskewed frame; magnitude still UNVERIFIED, carried over from the old camlink MOUNTS[52] table). mount_y_cm/mount_z_cm/lever_cm/parallax_k remain UNVERIFIED -- see _lever_parallax_note.
tovez._radio_note: No explicit override -- radio_address('tovez') falls through to make_deploy.derive_radio_from_name('tovez') = (55, 108), matching the MEASURED fleet table in .claude/rules/playfield-testing.md (2026-08-30).
tovez._lever_parallax_note: STILL A PLACEHOLDER. Added 2026-09-04 for sprint 029 ticket 007's bench session so field_dance.py could run at all (it requires both keys unconditionally). lever_cm=[0,0] is harmless for field_dance.py's PASS/FAIL: turn() only reads the heading delta (lever-independent) and drive() differences two poses taken at the same heading, so a constant-but-wrong lever cancels in the delta. parallax_k borrowed from vevov (tag height 11.8 cm vs tovez's 11.3 cm -- close enough for the dance's 3 cm tolerance). The dance FAILED that same session (large, inconsistent pivot/drive errors, not a clean convention offset) and evidence-gathering pointed at a suspected kernel wedge on tovez, not at these placeholders -- see captures/bench-acceptance-029-20260904/notes.md. No pivot-triple/translation-probe fit was attempted; do not trust these two values for a real distance/angle measurement until they are replaced with a MEASURED fit after tovez is recovered.
